reason: r23 fixes the field that explains all four runs where the gauge vanished. The mask's rectangle is derived state: its enter handler (main+0xa4ba94) rebuilds +0xb0..+0xbc from the node's quad whenever bit 1 of +0xa4 is set, which is what the game's own Size setter (main+0xa4ba40) raises, and then applies the box to the context. The quad builder main+0xa4b390 reads mask+0xa0's low 4 bits as two anchor modes: & 3 for y and & 0xc for x, where mode 0 spans 0..size, 1 centres, 2 spans -size..0, and 3 collapses the axis to zero extent. The class factory (main+0xa4b6cc) writes (word & 0xfffff000) | 0xff0, leaving bits 0-3 as the freshly allocated block had them; the class has no Anchor property in its DTI record, and the game's masks get their anchors from the row builder's resource record. A factory-built mask therefore keeps recycled anchor bits, and the x-collapsed / y-spanning signature (left == right, top = position, bottom = position + the height written) appears in r14 (0 0 W 32), r18 (376 of 383 lines), r20 (206 of 206) and r22 (225 of 225, with sharpness moving and the write happening every frame). r23 writes mask+0xa0 & !0xf and +0xa4 = 3 on every enter, so the game's own arithmetic produces the rectangle from the authored pair and position written in the same call; the rectangle words are no longer written. The probe now prints the anchor word. The insertion itself has completed three times (r18, r20, r22), each with the 5-word object array through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic, the class factory's object, and the native linkers. r22 also proved the walker's liveness check firing and re-arming once (t=591.98), which removes r18's writes into a freed mask. MHGU quests are split into areas with a loading screen between them (the tester's account of 2026-10-24), so the row, and with it the mask, is per area. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r23 sets the mask's anchor modes (mask+0xa0 bits 0-3 to 0) and lets the game's enter handler rebuild the rectangle. r22 ran on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes a18290a6df0b2cbe2edaf67e49a612a16540306f41c8cd38544c570729a69945): insertion completed, gauge missing from the quest start, 225 of 225 probe lines at left == right with sharpness moving, and the walker's links-lost line fired once and re-armed. r20 and r18 ran the same day with the same outcome. r17/r16/r15 ran clean; r14 ran once and crashed.

r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r23 has not been run. Four completed insertions (r14, r18, r20, r22) hid the gauge with a zero-width clip box; the anchor-mode fix is read from main+0xa4b390, main+0xa4b6cc and the class's DTI record, and no run has read the anchor word back.
